items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1961-06-28
items.q: Tony Jackson was a good pianist.

ctx.x: The very first ones you remember that worked in the district? Let's see.

They had another father there, but it was a good pianist. Well, maybe I can remember. I can't think of his name. Talking about Alfred Wilson. Alfred Wilson. Tony Jackson. Tony Jackson was a good pianist. Did you ever work? No. Did you ever work? No. Yeah, yeah. I never worked with them fellas. Robert Caldwell.

He was a sissified. He had a brother named George Collar. He was a shoemaker. He was a clarinet player. Uptown. Well Bob Caldwell, the district went down. He got a job working and why you working? With the bank when he jumped out the window. It was Bob Caldwell.

items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1972-04-05
items.q: He met Tony Jackson up there.

ctx.x: The woman would take me there like me and her good buddies. We'd go there and say, you want to get a suit? Come on, get your measure taken. Yeah. And I'm gonna get you a suit. And I'd go there with her, the tailor would take my measure, and she'd put ten dollars or fifteen, twenty dollars down on it. You see? Uh-huh. And get it out when it's made, you see? Uh-huh.
Well, one time Minetta was talking about going to Chicago. He met Tony Jackson up there. Yeah.
